about: Public-notice channels per operator or agency: pages, sites, feeds, lists and accounts through which the public is told of sewage discharges, by law, permit or voluntarily. Read by pipeline/ingest/notification_pages.py (schema and validator there; test tests/test_notice_channels.py).

channels.name: A&D Water Service Inc
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: A&D Water Service Inc: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: flow not checked: no design flow is on record for WQCSD0368 (a collection system or a plant missing from EPA's rows); listed on the side of caution. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

channels.name: A&D Water Service Inc
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(2): "In the event of a discharge of 15,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county in which the discharge occurs and in each county downstream from the point of discharge that is significantly affected by the discharge." The notice is captioned "NOTICE OF DISCHARGE OF UNTREATED SEWAGE" and published within 10 days after the Secretary approves its form, content and newspapers
channels.note: No web form: A&D Water Service Inc (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a paid notice in newspapers of the county and of each downstream county the Secretary finds significantly affected, for 15,000 gallons or more; proof of publication is filed with DEQ within 30 days. Printed only; the law requires no web posting. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: A&D Water Service Inc
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: A&D Water Service Inc (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Currituck Water and Sewer LLC
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(2): "In the event of a discharge of 15,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, publish a notice of the discharge in a newspaper having general circulation in the county in which the discharge occurs and in each county downstream from the point of discharge that is significantly affected by the discharge." channels.note: No web form: Currituck Water and Sewer LLC (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a paid notice in newspapers of the county and of each downstream county the Secretary finds significantly affected, for 15,000 gallons or more; proof of publication is filed with DEQ within 30 days. channels.name: Currituck Water and Sewer LLC
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. channels.note: No web form: Currituck Water and Sewer LLC (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.note: No web form: City of Elizabeth City: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: EPA's permitted (design) flow for NC0025011 is 4.5 MGD, over the threshold; the average annual flow the law counts was not checked. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: City of Lincolnton (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Town of Littleton
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Littleton: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: EPA's permitted (design) flow for NC0025691 is 0.28 MGD, over the threshold; the average annual flow the law counts was not checked. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Murfreesboro (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Town of Murphy
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Murphy: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: EPA's permitted (design) flow for NC0020940 is 1.4 MGD, over the threshold; the average annual flow the law counts was not checked. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

channels.name: Town of Ranlo
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(b)(1): "In the event of a discharge of 1,000 gallons or more of untreated wastewater to the surface waters of the State, issue a press release to all print and electronic news media that provide general coverage in the county where the discharge occurred setting out the details of the discharge. The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Ranlo (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

The owner or operator shall issue the press release within 24 hours after the owner or operator has determined that the discharge has reached the surface waters of the State."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Rutherfordton (municipal or domestic works, public or private, so (b)): a press release to all print and electronic news media covering the county within 24 hours after it determines that 1,000 gallons or more reached surface waters. It reaches the public printed only or on air, as the media carry it; the law requires no web posting. Copies and the media list are kept a year and given to any person on request. (G.S. 143-215.1C, read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04; research/nc/report.md §2.1)

channels.name: Town of Salemburg
channels.legal_basis: G.S. 143-215.1C(a): "The owner or operator of any wastewater collection or treatment works, the operation of which is primarily to collect or treat municipal or domestic wastewater and for which a permit is issued under this Part and having an average annual flow greater than 200,000 gallons per day, shall provide to the users or customers of the collection system or treatment works and to the Department an annual report that summarizes the performance of the collection system or treatment works and the extent to which the collection system or treatment works has violated the permit or federal or State laws, regulations, or rules related to the protection of water quality. The report shall be prepared on either a calendar or fiscal year basis and shall be provided no later than 60 days after the end of the calendar or fiscal year."
channels.note: No web form: Town of Salemburg: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: flow not checked: no design flow is on record for WQCSD0046 (a collection system or a plant missing from EPA's rows); listed on the side of caution. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)

channels.note: No web form: Water and Sewer Authority of Cabarrus County: the yearly report on the system's performance and its permit violations goes to the users or customers and a copy to the Department (DEQ), no later than 60 days after the calendar or fiscal year; the law requires no web posting. It summarizes the year, not single overflows. The duty applies to municipal or domestic works with an average annual flow over 200,000 gallons a day: EPA's permitted (design) flow for NC0036269 is 30 MGD, over the threshold; the average annual flow the law counts was not checked. The operator's own posting was not searched individually. (G.S. 143-215.1C(a), read on ncleg.gov 2026-11-04)
